raw: {"analysis": "Both responses provide comprehensive, well-structured plans addressing the key requirements: byte-stable output verification, test coverage, downstream impact, rollback, CI cost, flaky test handling, and coupling. WMF offers a clearer three-lane structure with explicitly numbered gates (1-4) and includes a dedicated cache stability verification gate in staging (processing 1,000 images twice) that directly validates the byte-stable requirement. Its rollback plan is more concrete (revert main branch, automated pipeline) and includes a post-landing cleanup step. ZNZ also covers all points but has an inconsistent gate numbering (G1, G3, G4...), a less explicit cache stability test (only mentions verifying CDN hit rates), and a slightly more ambiguous rollback (feature flag if available vs. direct swap). Both are strong, but WMF's plan is more actionable and leaves fewer follow-up questions.", "verdict": "WMF"}
